summary: The note describes the Battle of the Kentish Knock, a naval engagement during the First Anglo-Dutch War fought on 28 September 1652 (8 October Gregorian) between the Dutch Republic and England. It took place near the Kentish Knock shoal in the North Sea about thirty kilometres east of the Thames mouth. The Dutch fleet was internally divided and failed to mount a determined effort, so it soon withdrew after losing two ships and many casualties.
one_line: A 1652 naval battle in the First Anglo-Dutch War between the Dutch Republic and England near the Kentish Knock shoal in the North Sea.
key_facts: The Battle of the Kentish Knock was also called the Battle of the Zealand Approaches.
The battle was a naval battle between the fleets of the Dutch Republic and England.
The battle was fought on 28 September 1652 (8 October Gregorian calendar).
The battle took place during the First Anglo-Dutch War.
The battle was fought near the shoal called the Kentish Knock in the North Sea.
The Kentish Knock lies about thirty kilometres east of the mouth of the river Thames.
The Dutch fleet was internally divided on political, regional and personal grounds.
The Dutch fleet proved incapable of making a determined effort in the battle.
The Dutch fleet was soon forced to withdraw from the battle.
The Dutch fleet lost two ships in the battle.
The Dutch fleet suffered many casualties in the battle.
In Dutch the action is called the "Slag bij de Hoofden".
